import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 903

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/903](https://www.erdosproblems.com/903)
- [EFSW85] Erdős, P. and Fowler, Joel C. and S\'os, Vera T. and Wilson, Richard M., On {$2$}-designs.
  J. Combin. Theory Ser. A (1985), 131--142.
- [dBEr48] de Bruijn, N. G. and Erdős, P., On a combinatorial problem. Nederl. Akad. Wetensch.,
  Proc. (1948), 1277--1279 = Indagationes Math. 10, 421--423.
-/

namespace Erdos903

open Filter Asymptotics

/--
Let $n=p^2+p+1$ for some prime power $p$, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_t\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ be a
block design (so that every pair $x,y\in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ is contained in exactly one $A_i$). Is it
true that if $t>n$ then $t\geq n+p$?

This is true, and was proved by Erdős, Fowler, Sós, and Wilson [EFSW85].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_903 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, IsPrimePow p →
    ∀ H : Finset (Finset (Fin (p ^ 2 + p + 1))),
      H.IsPairwiseBalancedDesign → p ^ 2 + p + 1 < H.card →
        p ^ 2 + p + 1 + p ≤ H.card := by
  sorry

end Erdos903

reformulations.difference: The source describes indexed blocks A₁,…,Aₜ and unique containment of pairs of distinct points. Lean instead uses a finset of blocks, its cardinality, and unique containment of two-element finsets.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every block has at least two points. Repeating a block at two indices would therefore put a distinct pair in two indexed blocks, contradicting uniqueness. Consequently the indexed family is injective, and its image finset has cardinality t. Conversely, a finset can be enumerated without repetitions. Every two-element finset is {x,y} for distinct x,y, so the two pair-containment conditions coincide. The full equivalence of these formulations was proved as erdos903_representation_equivalence in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without relying on the problem theorem or sorryAx.

sources_consulted: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1985-22.pdf — Erdős, Fowler, Sós, and Wilson, On 2-Designs (1985), especially the definition on p. 131, Theorem 2 and remarks on pp. 132–133, and its proof.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1948-01.pdf — de Bruijn and Erdős, On a combinatorial problem (1948), Theorem 1 and accompanying discussion.
https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html — publication archive identifying both cited papers.
Mathlib/Algebra/IsPrimePow.lean — prime-power definition, natural-number specialization, and boundary restrictions.
could_not_verify: Erdos903.erdos_903: The exact prime-power restriction in the question posed at https://www.erdosproblems.com/903 could not be independently verified because the webpage and alternate routes returned Cloudflare challenges. The cited EFSW85 definition and bound were verified, but its Theorem 2 allows general integer p; that stronger theorem alone does not establish the exact quantifier scope of the webpage’s question.
review.notes: EFSW85 Theorem 2 excludes exactly n < t < n+p, and its definition explicitly requires blocks to have more than one point, matching Lean. The recorded positive answer and research-solved category agree with the paper and companion database. Lean checks confirmed that p=0,1 are excluded; at p=2, the Fano design has 7 blocks and splitting one line gives a valid 9-block design attaining the bound. Padding the Fano design with an empty or singleton block fails the design predicate. A whole-ground-set block forces the family to have only one block, so it cannot satisfy t>n.
